summary: Venus's 20-year mahadasha, the longest in the Vimshottari cycle, is described as a period of comfort, marriage and family celebration, vehicles, fine clothes, ornaments, wealth, the arts and royal favour when Venus is well placed. BPHS turns it toward quarrels with kin, trouble to the wife, business loss and separation from relatives when Venus is in the 6th, 8th or 12th, and toward bodily trouble when Venus rules the 2nd or 7th.
common_outcomes: fine clothes, ornaments, conveyances, cattle and land; sweet food daily; recognition from the ruler; music and dance at home by the grace of Lakshmi (BPHS 47.79-82, when Venus is exalted, in its own sign or in a kendra or trikona)
a wife, children, wealth, great comfort, garlands and perfumes, clothes, ornaments, vehicles, and fortune and fame like a king's (Jataka Parijata 18.158)

materials for pleasure and comfort, good vehicles, cows, gems, ornaments and treasure, enjoyment with young women, intellectual work, voyages, auspicious acts and gifts from the ruler (Phaladeepika 19.12)
a wife, jewels, clothes, treasure, horses and the comforts of bed and seat; wealth from trade, farming and voyages (Phaladeepika 19.26)
quarrels with kinsmen, distress to the wife, business losses, loss of cattle and separation from relatives when Venus is in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.83-84)
rare_outcomes: a kingdom or high government post, command of an army, marriages and births in the family, recovery of a lost position or property (BPHS 47.81-83, Venus in its moolatrikona)
rulership of a region or village, building temples and reservoirs, giving food in charity (BPHS 47.85-87, Venus in the 4th as 9th or 10th lord)
anxiety, mental distress, separation from or loss of parents and elders, and hardship to relatives (Phaladeepika 19.26)
gems, sharper intellect, great wealth and public praise (Phaladeepika 20.26, Venus strong in own or exaltation sign in the 10th, 11th or 12th)
[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] when Venus owns kendras and also owns or occupies the 2nd or 7th (Phaladeepika 20.50)

by_area.personality: Pleasure-seeking, intellectual and artistic pursuits (Phaladeepika 19.12); enthusiasm and vigour in work (BPHS 47.87); a period of strong sensuality when Venus is in Libra (Raman p. 276).
by_area.career: Recognition from the ruler, high government post, command of an army when Venus is strong (BPHS 47.79-83); rulership of a region or village as 9th or 10th lord in the 4th (BPHS 47.85-86); business losses when Venus is in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.84); promotion to responsible office with Venus in Pisces (Raman p. 277).
by_area.finance: Vehicles, clothes, ornaments, cattle and land (BPHS 47.79-80); wealth, treasure and gems (Jataka Parijata 18.158; Phaladeepika 19.12); income from trade, farming and voyages (Phaladeepika 19.26); loss of wealth and status if Venus is exalted in the rasi but debilitated in the navamsa (Jataka Parijata 18.168).
by_area.health: Bodily pain and trouble when Venus rules the 2nd or 7th (BPHS 47.88); Raman notes venereal trouble with Venus in Taurus and generative-organ trouble, arthritis and nervous strain with Venus in Virgo (pp. 275-276).
by_area.relationships: Marriage and a wife are central (Jataka Parijata 18.158; Phaladeepika 19.26; BPHS 47.82); distress to and harassment from the wife when Venus is in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.84-85); quarrels and separation with Venus in Virgo (Raman p. 276).
by_area.family: Births and marriages in the family, visits of friends (BPHS 47.81-82); happiness from wife and children (BPHS 47.87); enmity with kinsmen and separation from relatives when Venus is in a dusthana (BPHS 47.84-85); anxiety about parents and elders (Phaladeepika 19.26).
by_area.spirituality: Pious works such as building temples and reservoirs and giving grain in charity (BPHS 47.86-87); religious and philosophical study with Venus in Sagittarius (Raman p. 277).

strengtheners: Venus exalted, in its own sign, or in a kendra or trikona (BPHS 47.79)
Venus in the 4th (Sanskrit: lagna or 4th) as lord of the 9th or 10th (BPHS 47.85)
Venus strong, not combust, free of malefics, in its own or exaltation sign falling in the 10th, 11th or 12th (Phaladeepika 20.26)
Venus debilitated in the rasi but exalted in the navamsa (Jataka Parijata 18.169)
Venus yogakaraka for Capricorn and Aquarius lagnas, and lord of the 2nd and 9th for Virgo lagna (Santhanam's note to BPHS 47.89)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.83); the Sanskrit adds debilitation
Venus owning kendras (kendradhipati dosha), worse if it also owns or occupies the 2nd or 7th (Phaladeepika 20.50)
Venus exalted in the rasi but debilitated in the navamsa (Jataka Parijata 18.168)
lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS judges the dasha from the lagna: the house Venus occupies, its dignity, and its lordship of the 2nd/7th (maraka) or 9th/10th. Santhanam notes Venus is yogakaraka for Capricorn and Aquarius lagnas and very auspicious for Virgo lagna. Phaladeepika 20.50 says Venus, like Jupiter, is harmed by kendra lordship and becomes a strong maraka if it also owns or occupies the 2nd or 7th. BPHS 47.88 says the same results appear in Venus's own sub-period, and in the other sub-periods according to the sub-lords' strength. Raman reads results by Venus's sign (pp. 275-277). Modern method notes: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao uses the Sun as a reference point for a mahadasha, the Moon for an antardasha and the dasha lord as a temporary lagna for its sub-periods; Frawley stresses the dasha lord's lordship and aspects. No source read gives a Venus-specific rule counted from the Moon.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.78-89, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 588-589
source_views.view: Venus exalted, own sign, kendra or trikona: clothes, ornaments, conveyances, cattle and land, daily sweets, royal recognition, songs and dances by Lakshmi's grace. In moolatrikona: kingdom or high post, a house, children and grandchildren, marriages, army command, friends' visits, recovery of lost position. In the 6th, 8th or 12th: enmity of kinsmen, distress to wife, business loss, cattle destroyed, separation from relations. In the 4th as lord of the 9th or 10th: rulership of a region or village, pious works, charity, fame, happiness from wife and children. Same results in its own sub-period. Lord of the 2nd or 7th: bodily pain; remedy Shatarudriya or Mrityunjaya japa and the gift of a cow or female buffalo.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.78-89, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Verse 79 adds deep exaltation and coronation. Verse 83 lists the 6th, 8th or 12th, or debilitated, or in the sign of loss. Verse 85 reads 'in the lagna or the 4th sign, by lordship of the 9th and 10th'. Verse 88: in its own bhukti these results, in other bhuktis according to their strength; as 2nd/7th lord bodily trouble. Verse 89: recite the Rudra or Tryambaka mantra and give a white cow or a buffalo, after which health returns.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 19.12 and 19.26 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib; 19.26 marked not proofread)
source_views.view: 19.12: things for pleasure and comfort, good vehicles, cows, gems, ornaments, treasure, enjoyment with young women, intellectual pursuits, voyages, auspicious acts, gifts from the ruler. 19.26: a wife, jewels, clothes, treasure, horses, comforts; wealth from trade, farming and voyages; but anxiety, mental distress, separation from or loss of parents and elders, and hardship to relatives.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.26 and 20.50 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri; siva.sh)
source_views.view: 20.26: Venus in its own or exaltation sign, not combust, not with a malefic, in the 10th, 11th or 12th gives gems, sharp intellect, great wealth and public praise. 20.50: Jupiter and Venus are harmful as kendra lords and become powerful death-inflicting planets if they also own or occupy the 2nd or 7th.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.158, 18.168-169 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri vol. 2, pp. 1071, 1075; 18.168 is printed as a second 169)
source_views.view: Venus's dasa gives a wife, children, wealth, great comfort, garlands, clothes, ornaments, vehicles, and fortune and fame like a king's. Venus exalted but in its debilitation navamsa: loss of wealth and status. Venus debilitated but in its exaltation navamsa: success in farming and trade and more wealth as the dasa ripens.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 230-233, 275-277
source_views.view: Gives results by Venus's sign: Aries palatial living, fame, a child; Taurus great ease and pleasure, sea travel, debts cleared, venereal trouble; Gemini gain of territory, vehicles, marital harmony; Cancer grief, loss of property and wealth, quarrels with relatives; Leo mental sorrow, danger from fire and poison, exile, illness of spouse or child; Virgo marital quarrels and separation, mortgaged property, genital and nervous troubles; Libra fame, royal patronage, luxury; Scorpio hatred, risks, loss of wealth; Sagittarius fame, religious study, success; Capricorn foreign travel, learning, success; Aquarius new property, books, honours, domestic harmony; Pisces political power, promotion, charity, domestic happiness. General rules: results vary with the dasa lord's strength, house, sign, aspects and navamsa, and are modified by transits.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers ch. 6, pp. 199-203
source_views.view: Lists the sub-periods of Venus's 20-year dasa. General method only: the major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects; the relationship between major and minor lords is magnified, with 6/8/12 placements from each other working badly, trines and quadrants well, and friendship or enmity adjusting the outcome.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, sec. 16.5, pp. 214-215
source_views.view: General method only: each planet gives what it indicates in the divisional charts in its dasas; the Sun is the key reference for a mahadasha, the Moon for an antardasha, the lagna for a pratyantardasha, and the dasa lord can serve as a temporary lagna for its antardashas.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998)
source_views.view: Case studies only, no general rules for Venus's dasa: Rath reads Venus-period events through house lordship in divisional charts (vehicles from D-16, education from D-24, parents from D-12) and prescribes the mantra of the planet's deity as a remedy.

disagreements: BPHS 47.85: Santhanam has Venus 'in the 4th' as 9th or 10th lord, while the Sanskrit reads 'in the lagna or the 4th'. BPHS 47.83: the Sanskrit adds debilitation to the 6/8/12 condition, Santhanam omits it. BPHS 47.89 remedy: Santhanam gives Shatarudriya or Mrityunjaya japa, the Sanskrit gloss gives the Rudra or Tryambaka mantra. Both prescribe giving a (white) cow or a buffalo. Phaladeepika 19.26 adds anxiety and loss of parents and elders, which the other classical texts do not mention. Raman's sign-by-sign results make Cancer, Leo, Virgo and Scorpio bad, which follows no dignity rule in BPHS (Cancer and Leo are not Venus's debilitation).
phrasing_guidance: Frame the Venus period as a long chapter centred on comfort, relationships, family events, possessions and the arts. Its tone depends on Venus's house, dignity and lordship. Where the chart shows the weak conditions, speak of strain in close relationships and money, and of keeping balance in pleasures. Never predict death, the loss of a parent or a specific illness; for the maraka rule, speak only of a time to look after health.
